[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "title": "3D Kinematic Vectors: Position, Displacement, Velocity, and Acceleration",
    "scope": "Introduces vector descriptions of motion in Cartesian coordinates, defining the position vector and displacement across intervals. Establishes average and instantaneous velocity as calculus derivatives, highlighting geometric tangency to the trajectory. Formulates instantaneous acceleration arising from changes in magnitude, direction, or both, demonstrated via polynomial coordinate trajectories.",
    "key_points": [
      "Position vector r(t) = x(t)i + y(t)j + z(t)k and displacement Delta r = r_2 - r_1 = Delta x i + Delta y j + Delta z k",
      "Average velocity v_avg = Delta r / Delta t, sharing the exact direction of displacement Delta r",
      "Instantaneous velocity v = dr/dt = (dx/dt)i + (dy/dt)j + (dz/dt)k, always tangent to the trajectory path",
      "Instantaneous acceleration a = dv/dt = (dv_x/dt)i + (dv_y/dt)j + (dv_z/dt)k, non-zero when velocity changes magnitude, direction, or both",
      "Worked polynomial trajectory: x(t) = -0.31t^2 + 7.2t + 28, y(t) = 0.22t^2 - 9.1t + 30; at t = 15 s, v_x = -2.1 m/s, v_y = -2.5 m/s, v = (-2.1 m/s)i + (-2.5 m/s)j oriented at -130 degrees"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "title": "Projectile Motion: Orthogonal Independence and Parabolic Trajectories",
    "scope": "Examines two-dimensional motion under constant downward gravitational acceleration with negligible air resistance. Establishes the Galilean principle of independent orthogonal motions, decoupling horizontal uniform motion from vertical free fall. Derives the algebraic trajectory equation, horizontal range formula, and flight duration relationships for complementary launch angles.",
    "key_points": [
      "Independence of orthogonal motions: horizontal motion has zero acceleration (a_x = 0), vertical motion has constant downward acceleration (a_y = -g)",
      "Parametric kinematic equations: x - x_0 = (v_0 cos theta_0)t and y - y_0 = (v_0 sin theta_0)t - (1/2)gt^2",
      "Path equation elimination of t: y = (tan theta_0)x - [g / (2(v_0 cos theta_0)^2)]x^2, proving a parabolic trajectory",
      "Horizontal range on flat ground: R = (v_0^2 / g) sin(2 theta_0)",
      "Range symmetry and flight time: complementary angles (30 degrees and 60 degrees) yield the same range R, but flight duration t = (2 v_0 sin theta_0)/g is sqrt(3) times longer for 60 degrees"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "title": "Uniform Circular Motion and Centripetal Acceleration",
    "scope": "Details kinematics of a particle traversing a circular path at constant speed, where acceleration is purely directional. Deduces centripetal acceleration via Cartesian coordinate differentiation, proving its magnitude and strict radially inward orientation. Connects speed, orbital radius, and period of revolution, concluding with acceleration limits and physiological g-LOC thresholds.",
    "key_points": [
      "Uniform circular motion definition: constant speed v with continuously changing direction of velocity",
      "Velocity components: v = (-v sin theta)i + (v cos theta)j = [-v(y_p/r)]i + [v(x_p/r)]j",
      "Time differentiation of velocity: a = dv/dt = [-(v^2/r)cos theta]i + [-(v^2/r)sin theta]j, giving magnitude a = v^2/r",
      "Vector direction: tan phi = a_y / a_x = tan theta, proving acceleration points radially inward toward the center",
      "Period of revolution T = 2 pi r / v, yielding the acceleration relation a = 2 pi v / T",
      "Top Gun high-g turn analysis: initial velocity v_i = 400i + 500j m/s reverses to v_f = -400i - 500j m/s in 24 s; T = 48 s, v = 640.31 m/s, yielding a = 83.81 m/s^2 approx 8.6g (exceeding the ~4g tunnel vision and g-LOC threshold)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "title": "Natural Coordinates: Tangential and Normal Acceleration",
    "scope": "Formulates general curvilinear motion using intrinsic Frenet path coordinates defined by unit tangent and normal vectors. Derives the separation of total acceleration into the tangential component governing speed changes and the normal component governing curvature. Uses differential geometry of similar triangles on infinitesimal arc elements to deduce the centripetal relation.",
    "key_points": [
      "Velocity representation in natural frame: V(t) = v(t) tau(t), where speed is the arc length derivative v = dl/dt",
      "Full acceleration decomposition: a = dV/dt = (dv/dt)tau + v(d tau/dt) = a_tau + a_n",
      "Tangential acceleration a_tau = (dv/dt)tau, collinear with velocity and modifying speed",
      "Normal acceleration a_n = v(d tau/dt) = (v^2 / rho)n, directed along principal normal n toward the center of curvature",
      "Geometric proof: d tau perp tau and d tau / tau = dl / rho as dl -> 0 with |tau| = 1, leading to d tau / dl = 1 / rho",
      "Total acceleration magnitude: a = sqrt(a_tau^2 + a_n^2)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "title": "Vector Decomposition of Acceleration and Trajectory Curvature",
    "scope": "Translates intrinsic accelerations into Cartesian coordinate and vector dot/cross product expressions for arbitrary 2D motion. Establishes algebraic formulas for projecting acceleration along and orthogonal to the velocity vector. Defines trajectory curvature and radius of curvature from kinematic vectors, demonstrated on an analytically prescribed velocity field.",
    "key_points": [
      "Tangential acceleration vector: a_tau = [(a . v) / (v . v)] v = [(a_x v_x + a_y v_y) / (v_x^2 + v_y^2)](v_x i + v_y j), with scalar |a_tau| = (a . v) / v",
      "Normal acceleration vector: a_n = a - a_tau = [(a_x v_y - a_y v_x) / (v_x^2 + v_y^2)](v_y i - v_x j)",
      "Normal acceleration scalar magnitude: a_n = sqrt(a^2 - a_tau^2) = |a_x v_y - a_y v_x| / v = |a x v| / v",
      "Curvature rho = 1/R = a_n / v^2 = |a_x v_y - a_y v_x| / v^3 = |a x v| / v^3",
      "Radius of curvature formula: R = v^3 / |a_x v_y - a_y v_x|",
      "Curvature radius example: particle with v = a i + bx j from origin has trajectory y(x) = bx^2 / (2a), acceleration a_x = 0, a_y = ab, and R(x) = (a/b)[1 + (bx/a)^2]^(3/2)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "title": "Pursuit Dynamics: Symmetric Systems and Straight-Line Tracking",
    "scope": "Explores pursuit kinematics beginning with baseline 1D relative closing-speed principles and extending to symmetric multi-agent configurations. Formulates the closing rate along the line of sight using velocity projections. Analyzes the cyclic pursuit of three particles at equilateral triangle vertices, setting up differential equations for edge contraction and determining convergence time.",
    "key_points": [
      "1D collinear pursuit: relative closing speed Delta v = v_C - v_A, capture time t = S / (v_C - v_A)",
      "Line-of-sight closing rate: -dl/dt equals the sum of velocity projections of pursuer and target along their connecting segment",
      "Cyclic pursuit on an equilateral triangle: three points with equal constant speeds v continually pursue each other in cyclic order",
      "Projection of target velocity along the side: v_(2,G) = v cos(pi/3) = v / 2 directed toward the pursuer",
      "Edge length contraction ODE: -dl/dt = |v_1| + |v_(2,G)| = v + (v/2) = (3/2)v",
      "Convergence time integration: -int_a^0 dl = (3/2)v int_0^t dt' yields t = 2a / (3v)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "title": "Orthogonal Target Pursuit: Analytical Invariants and Numerical ODE Solutions",
    "scope": "Analyzes classical pure pursuit where pursuer A moves at constant speed v aiming continuously at target B traveling rectilinearly at speed u < v with initially perpendicular velocities. Derives the closed-form analytical convergence time using projection onto the instantaneous line of sight combined with horizontal coordinate tracking. Establishes the corresponding non-linear state-space ODE system used for numerical simulations.",
    "key_points": [
      "Coordinate setup: target B at (ut, 0) moving along x-axis; pursuer A starts at (0, -l) with velocity unit vector directed along segment AB",
      "Distance along line of sight: AB(t) = l - int_0^t [v - u cos(alpha(t'))] dt', reaching zero at convergence time T",
      "Target coordinate identity: total x-displacement Delta x_B(T) = uT matches pursuer x-displacement int_0^T v cos(alpha(t')) dt', yielding int_0^T cos(alpha(t')) dt' = uT / v",
      "Exact convergence time derivation: l = vT - u(uT / v) = T(v^2 - u^2)/v, resulting in T = vl / (v^2 - u^2)",
      "State-space ODE system: dX_A/dt = v (X_B - X_A) / sqrt((X_B - X_A)^2 + Y_A^2), dY_A/dt = sqrt(v^2 - (dX_A/dt)^2), solved numerically via Mathcad Odesolve",
      "Numerical and analytical agreement: for u = 1 m/s, v = 2 m/s, l = 10 m, both methods yield convergence time T = 6.7 s at Y_A(T) = 0"
    ]
  }
]
